steps_basic.title: Open Scratch and create project
steps_basic.instruction: Open Scratch and click Create. You should see the Stage and a sprite (cat).
steps_basic.hint: Go to scratch.mit.edu and click the Create button at the top.

steps_basic.title: Choose your character
steps_basic.instruction: Delete the Cat sprite (right-click → delete) OR keep it and rename it 'Buddy' by clicking on the sprite name box.
steps_basic.hint: Right-click on the cat sprite in the sprite list and choose 'delete', or just rename it.

steps_basic.title: Add click event
steps_basic.instruction: Click Buddy so it is selected (blue outline). Then drag 'when this sprite clicked' from Events into the coding area.
steps_basic.hint: Events category (yellow blocks) → 'when this sprite clicked'

steps_basic.title: Make Buddy speak
steps_basic.instruction: From Looks, drag 'say [Hi! I'm Buddy!] for (2) seconds' and snap it under the event block.
steps_basic.hint: Looks category (purple blocks) → say [ ] for ( ) seconds
steps_basic.blocks_text:
when this sprite clicked
say [Hi! I'm Buddy!] for (2) seconds

steps_basic.title: Test your character
steps_basic.instruction: Click Buddy on the stage to test. Buddy should speak! If it works, you're done with Basic level!
steps_basic.hint: Click on Buddy in the big stage area (right side of screen).
steps_basic.blocks_text:
when this sprite clicked
say [Hi! I'm Buddy!] for (2) seconds

steps_standard.title: Start with Basic code
steps_standard.instruction: Great! You've unlocked Standard level. You'll now add costume changes and sounds. Make sure you have the Basic code working first.
steps_standard.hint: You should have: 'when this sprite clicked' → 'say [Hi! I'm Buddy!] for (2) seconds'
steps_standard.blocks_text:
when this sprite clicked
say [Hi! I'm Buddy!] for (2) seconds

steps_standard.title: Add a second costume
steps_standard.instruction: Click the Costumes tab at the top. Add or duplicate a second costume so you have costume1 and costume2.
steps_standard.hint: Click 'Costumes' tab → hover over costume → click duplicate icon, or choose a new costume.

steps_standard.title: Add more messages
steps_standard.instruction: Back to Code tab. Add two more 'say [ ] for ( ) seconds' blocks, so you have 3 total say blocks.
steps_standard.hint: Looks → say [ ] for ( ) seconds. Drag it 2 more times and stack them.
steps_standard.blocks_text:
when this sprite clicked
say [Hi! I'm Buddy!] for (2) seconds
say [How are you?] for (2) seconds
say [Nice to see you!] for (2) seconds

steps_standard.title: Add costume change
steps_standard.instruction: Insert 'switch costume to [costume2]' between message 1 and message 2.
steps_standard.hint: Looks → switch costume to [costume2]. Put it after the first say block.
steps_standard.blocks_text:
when this sprite clicked
say [Hi! I'm Buddy!] for (2) seconds
switch costume to [costume2 v]
say [How are you?] for (2) seconds
say [Nice to see you!] for (2) seconds

steps_standard.title: Choose a sound
steps_standard.instruction: Click the Sounds tab. Choose a sound (e.g., Pop) from the sound library.
steps_standard.hint: Sounds tab → click the speaker icon to choose a sound → select 'Pop' or any sound you like.

steps_standard.title: Add sound effect
steps_standard.instruction: Back to Code. From Sound category, add 'start sound [Pop]' after the last message.
steps_standard.blocks_text:
when this sprite clicked
say [Hi! I'm Buddy!] for (2) seconds
switch costume to [costume2 v]
say [How are you?] for (2) seconds
say [Nice to see you!] for (2) seconds
start sound [Pop v]

steps_standard.title: Test Standard features
steps_standard.instruction: Click Buddy. You should see: message1 → costume change → message2 → message3 → sound. Works? You're ready for Advanced!
steps_standard.hint: The costume should change and you should hear a sound at the end.
steps_standard.blocks_text:
when this sprite clicked
say [Hi! I'm Buddy!] for (2) seconds
switch costume to [costume2 v]
say [How are you?] for (2) seconds
say [Nice to see you!] for (2) seconds
start sound [Pop v]

steps_advanced.title: Start with Standard code
steps_advanced.instruction: Awesome! You've reached Advanced level. You'll now add smart responses that change randomly and respond to the user's name.
steps_advanced.hint: You should have costume changes, multiple messages, and a sound effect already working.

steps_advanced.title: Create message variable
steps_advanced.instruction: Go to Variables and make a new variable called 'message' (for all sprites).
steps_advanced.hint: Variables → Make a Variable → type 'message' → For all sprites → OK

steps_advanced.title: Set random message number
steps_advanced.instruction: Near the top of your script (after 'when this sprite clicked'), add: set [message] to (pick random 1 to 3).
steps_advanced.hint: Variables → set [message] to. Operators → pick random (1) to (3). Put them together.
steps_advanced.blocks_text:
when this sprite clicked
set [message v] to (pick random (1) to (3))

steps_advanced.title: Ask for user's name
steps_advanced.instruction: Add 'ask [What is your name?] and wait' after setting the message variable.
steps_advanced.hint: Sensing → ask [What is your name?] and wait
steps_advanced.blocks_text:
when this sprite clicked
set [message v] to (pick random (1) to (3))
ask [What is your name?] and wait

steps_advanced.title: Join name with greeting
steps_advanced.instruction: Use Operators 'join [Hello ] (answer)' and put it into your first 'say' block instead of the fixed text.
steps_advanced.hint: Operators → join [Hello ] (answer). Drag it into the say block where the text goes.
steps_advanced.blocks_text:
when this sprite clicked
set [message v] to (pick random (1) to (3))
ask [What is your name?] and wait
say (join [Hello ] (answer)) for (2) seconds

steps_advanced.title: Add if-then for random replies
steps_advanced.instruction: Add 'if then' block. Inside the condition: (message) = (1). Inside the 'then': put reply #1.
steps_advanced.hint: Control → if then. Operators → (message) = (1). Put your say blocks inside.
steps_advanced.blocks_text:
when this sprite clicked
set [message v] to (pick random (1) to (3))
ask [What is your name?] and wait
if <(message) = (1)> then
  say (join [Hello ] (answer)) for (2) seconds
  say [Great to meet you!] for (2) seconds

steps_advanced.title: Add conditions for other messages
steps_advanced.instruction: Add else-if blocks for message=2 and message=3 with different replies for each.
steps_advanced.hint: Click + on if block to add else. Create separate responses for each random number.
steps_advanced.blocks_text:
when this sprite clicked
set [message v] to (pick random (1) to (3))
ask [What is your name?] and wait
if <(message) = (1)> then
  say (join [Hello ] (answer)) for (2) seconds
  say [Great to meet you!] for (2) seconds
else
  if <(message) = (2)> then
    say (join [Hi there, ] (answer)) for (2) seconds
    say [Welcome!] for (2) seconds
  else
    say (join [Hey ] (answer)) for (2) seconds
    say [Nice name!] for (2) seconds

steps_advanced.title: Test random smart responses
steps_advanced.instruction: Click Buddy several times. The replies should change randomly each time and include your name. Works? Advanced complete!
steps_advanced.hint: Each time you click, you should get a different greeting (1, 2, or 3) with your name.
